Attached is an initial draft of a short Q&A and a CSV export of our current subprocessor roster. The ask from your side was that the language be plain-English and suitable for procurement/legal reviewers who may not be privacy specialists.

Can Laura and Neha take a first pass to simplify the legal phrasing and produce a ~150–200 word snippet for the Console plus 6–8 quick Q&A bullets for sales/procurement? I suggest we keep one canonical public snippet and a slightly longer FAQ the sales team can share.

Thanks Priyom — quick pass attached and pasted below. Kept it intentionally short and neutral.

Public snippet (Console, ~110 words):
Redwood hosts inference for customers on dedicated and shared infrastructure. We only process customer data to provide the service; we don’t use it to train models. We rely on a small set of subprocessors (e.g., cloud providers, logging, and metrics vendors) to operate the platform. We maintain a current subprocessor list in the Console and provide manual options for customers with stricter residency or contractual requirements. Cross-border transfers are protected by contractual safeguards (standard contractual clauses and equivalent measures) — contact your account team for country-specific controls.

FAQ bullets (short answers for procurement):
- Which subprocessors do you use? — See Console subprocessor list (link).
- Can data be kept in a region? — Yes; hosted customers can select region-specific deployment options where available.
- Do you use customer data to train models? — No, customer data is not used for model training unless contractually agreed.
- What telemetry do you collect? — We collect minimal operational metadata (latency, error rates, token counts) used only for service reliability and billing.

I left a couple of flagged items in the draft where Neha should confirm the CSV entries.

Laura

2) For telemetry, we need an explicit list of the specific metrics collected (e.g., token counts, request timestamps, error codes) and confirmation that request bodies are not retained for training.
3) If you could include one-line guidance on how a customer requests subprocessor evidence (SOC2 reports, data processing addendum), that would be helpful.

Emma — appreciate the prompt review. We've updated the draft to include the three items below. Latest draft is attached and I'll push the Console snippet to the staging site for a quick UX check tomorrow morning.

Concise additions (for the Console snippet):
- Retention: Generated outputs (responses) are retained for up to 30 days by default for debugging and fraud detection; customers can request shorter retention via an account preference or by contract. Operational logs (error traces, token counts) are retained for up to 90 days to support reliability and billing.
- Telemetry: We collect request and response timestamps, per-request token counts, HTTP error codes, and anonymized usage aggregates. We do not use prompt or response content to train models unless a customer opts in via an explicit agreement.
- Evidence and requests: Customers may request subprocessors’ compliance reports and related evidence through the Console’s Trust center or by emailing privacy-requests@redwood.com; we typically respond within 5 business days and will provide SOC 2 summaries and DPA addenda where applicable.
